title: Amino acid analysis by HPLC with FLD detector
protocol: Hydrolyze purified protein with 6N HCl for 24 hours at 120°C in an oil bath.
Derivatize the resultant mixture with OPA for amino acid analysis.
Use a fluorescent detector (FLD) to analyze the derivatized sample on an Agilent 1260 HPLC system.
Apply FMOC-Cl to derivatize the sample for proline and hydroxyproline identification.
Load 50 μl of the derivatized sample onto a ZORBAX-SB-C-18 column (250×4.6m, 5 micron particle size).
Elute the column using a gradient elution method with 0.01M Na2HPO4 buffer and acetonitrile as mobile phase solvents.
Maintain the flow rate at 1 ml/min during elution.
Collect and evaluate data from the HPLC system using Agilent openLAB control panel software.
Quantify amino acid content via comparison to retention time and absorbance of standards.
Reconstitute OPA with 5 mg in methanol.
Add 50 microliters of sodium borate buffer to the mixture.
Add 450 microliters of sodium borate buffer to complete the OPA solution.
Mix an equal volume of hydrolyzed sample with the prepared OPA solution.
Incubate the mixed solution for two minutes at room temperature.
Prepare FMOC-Cl solution by diluting in acetone to a concentration of 10 µmol/mL.
Hydrolyze collagen sample \(20 µL of 1 mg/ml) and mix with 80 µL borate buffer \(20 µmol/mL, pH 10.5).
Add 100 µL of FMOC-Cl solution to the mixture.
Incubate the resultant mixture at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Add 300 µL of pentane to the mixture after incubation.
Extract excess FMOC-Cl and hydrolyzed product using pentane from the mixture.
Prepare the derivatized COLII sample by removing pentane, leaving it ready for HPLC injection.
